title: Paranal and the streaking stars
caption: Star trails over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars streak across the night sky, and far off on a mountaintop sits ESO's Paranal Observatory. The streaks are not a flaw in the picture but the point of it.

This effect comes from a very long exposure. While the camera's shutter stayed open, Earth kept rotating, and the camera turned with it. Each star, which to the eye would be a steady point, was drawn out into a line tracing its apparent path across the sky.

Photographs like this show the slow, steady turning of the sky as the night goes on, which we never see directly. The observatory in the distance turns with the Earth along with the camera, so only the sky, far beyond our planet, appears to move. The longer the shutter stays open, the longer each trail becomes.

understand.summary: This is a very long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only a very long exposure records their apparent motion as streaks.
